title: The first-return map is an exact symplectomorphism and the boundary first-return time is a boundary integral
author: Alberto Abbondandolo; Christian Lange; Marco Mazzucchelli
work: Higher systolic inequalities for 3-dimensional contact manifolds
source_version: Journal de l'École polytechnique — Mathématiques 9 (2022), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.195
difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `l:return_time_map` at source lines 1462-1472, a two-part statement: the first-return map is an exact symplectomorphism with phi^* nu = nu + d tau, and on the boundary the first-return time equals one plus the integral of nu along the projected orbit. The proof (source lines 1474-1493) proves the two parts by different mechanisms: the exactness is an explicit pull-back computation along the Reeb flow in which the term phi^*(tilde-lambda(R_{tilde lambda})) d tau is what makes the result exact (lines 1475-1478), whereas the boundary formula requires recognising the curve zeta_z(s) = (phi_s(z), s) as a reparametrisation of a Reeb orbit that winds once around the circle factor (lines 1479-1483) and then splitting the normalised form into ds plus the pull-back of nu (lines 1485-1490). The two labelled inputs are consumed only at the last line, which is why the lemma is normally read together with the normalisation result.
